Ashe.escape: Ashe has no mobility ability to create distance on her own, so engage when Ashe W Volley is down and Ashe Q Ranger’s Focus is inactive. If Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow is down, the risk of getting stunned is also lower. Close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence or bring an ally in with Thresh W Dark Passage, then use Thresh E Flay to block Ashe’s escape direction.
Ashe.build: Buy armor first to mitigate Ashe’s main damage. Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow deals magic damage, so armor won’t stop it. Since Ashe relies on basic attacks and attack speed for her damage, reducing her attack speed is also effective.
Ashe.combo: At close range, pull Ashe toward your allies with Thresh E Flay, then throw Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Thresh Q Death Sentence hits first, get an auto attack in, then use Thresh E Flay as the stun ends to give your allies time to follow up. Before recasting Thresh Q Death Sentence to go in, check that your allies can follow, and if needed, block Ashe’s escape route with Thresh R The Box.
Ashe.fight: Trade right after Ashe W Volley is down, while Ashe Q Ranger’s Focus is inactive. Instead of walking up in the open and throwing Thresh Q Death Sentence, look for an angle from brush where you can’t be seen, or wait until Ashe is locked into an action. If you get close, disrupt her movement with Thresh E Flay, then land Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Ashe.laning: Take control of the brush first to create an unseen angle for Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Ashe uses Ashe W Volley to contest the brush, fall back, protect your carry’s CS, and collect souls. Don’t risk walking out for a soul within Ashe’s attack range; collect it with Thresh W Dark Passage or leave it.
Ashe.phase: Early on, Thresh can start fights with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing Ashe out of lane and collecting souls instead of forcing a kill. In the mid game, look for times when Ashe W Volley and Ashe Q Ranger’s Focus are down, then engage with your allies. Thresh’s durability in the late game depends on the souls he has collected, so keep collecting them around fights and jungle camps after laning phase.
Ashe.teamfight: If your allies can engage first, catch Ashe, who has no mobility, with Thresh Q Death Sentence and block her escape with Thresh R The Box. If your team is fighting from the back, hold Thresh Q Death Sentence and use Thresh E Flay to peel enemies off your carry. Be ready to shield your allies and provide an escape route with Thresh W Dark Passage in case Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow puts them in danger.
Ashe.watch: Ashe W Volley slows in a cone, so dodge by moving sideways. Ashe P Frost Shot refreshes its slow with every basic attack, so don’t stay within her attack range for long. Keep your distance while Ashe Q Ranger’s Focus is active, and don’t start a small fight out of vision while Ashe R Enchanted Crystal Arrow is available.

Bard.phase: Early on, Thresh can start fights with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing the enemy out of lane and stacking souls rather than getting kills. Keep collecting souls through the mid and late game to build up Thresh P Damnation. The information provided isn’t enough to determine which champion is stronger at each stage of the game against Bard.
Bard.watch: Bard Q Cosmic Binding stuns if it hits a wall or a second target, so don’t stand with your back to a wall or in a line with an ally or minion. Watch for Bard E Magical Journey letting him flank you, and keep the damage immunity from Bard R Tempered Fate in mind.
Bard.build: Build a Null-Magic Mantle early to hold up, and choose Mercury’s Treads. Bard’s damage is mostly magic, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so raise your magic resistance first. If the healing from Bard W Caretaker’s Shrine can prolong fights, get an Oblivion Orb for Grievous Wounds.
Bard.combo: After Bard E Magical Journey is down, if Thresh Q Death Sentence hits, auto attack, then pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay as the stun is about to end. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block his escape. Only use the deep engage combo by recasting Thresh Q Death Sentence when you can bring an ally in immediately with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Bard.escape: The moment after Bard uses Bard E Magical Journey is your window to engage. Position yourself so you aren’t aligned with a wall, an ally, or a minion, allowing you to avoid the stun from Bard Q Cosmic Binding. Close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence, then follow with Thresh E Flay.
Bard.fight: Close the gap and fight immediately after forcing Bard to use Bard E Magical Journey. If you get close, disrupt his movement first with Thresh E Flay, then throw Thresh Q Death Sentence. Save your auto attacks until just before the trade, then land them one at a time.
Bard.laning: Take control of the brush first and look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from an unseen angle. If you lose the brush, collect souls and protect your carry’s CS. Collect souls within the enemy’s range with Thresh W Dark Passage, and leave them if it’s dangerous.
Bard.teamfight: If your team is fighting from the back, hold Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, target an enemy in the back line with Thresh Q Death Sentence. Targets caught in Bard R Tempered Fate are immune to damage, so account for that when chaining abilities. Place the walls of Thresh R The Box along the escape route to slow the chase.

Blitzcrank.fight: Trade right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses. Against an enemy who gets close, pull them first with Thresh E Flay, then throw Thresh Q Death Sentence. Even if Thresh Q Death Sentence hits, don’t recast it to go in if your allies can’t follow from your position.
Blitzcrank.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Build magic resistance first to protect against Blitzcrank’s main damage from Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab and Blitzcrank R Static Field.
Blitzcrank.combo: When Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab is down, land Thresh Q Death Sentence and auto attack, then pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block his escape.
Blitzcrank.escape: Engage right after Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab misses or when he has run out of mana and can’t use the grab. If Blitzcrank E Power Fist and Blitzcrank R Static Field have also been used, close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence and hold him with Thresh E Flay.
Blitzcrank.laning: Don’t stand side by side with minions; stay behind them to block Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab. Get vision of the brush, then look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from an unseen angle. Collect souls in dangerous spots with Thresh W Dark Passage or leave them.
Blitzcrank.teamfight: If your team is fighting from the back, hold Thresh Q Death Sentence and peel the enemy off with Thresh E Flay. Cast Thresh W Dark Passage before an ally is in danger to give them a shield and an escape route. If your allies engage first, don’t fixate on Blitzcrank; target the ally behind him with Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Blitzcrank.watch: Blitzcrank Q Rocket Grab pulls the first target it hits, so keep minions between you and Blitzcrank. When you don’t have vision of the brush, it’s hard to tell how far his grab can reach, so stay away from the brush. If you get pulled, Blitzcrank E Power Fist can knock you up, followed by the silence from Blitzcrank R Static Field.

Alistar.teamfight: While Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, don’t spend abilities hitting Alistar; target the damage dealers behind him. If you need to protect your carry, push away an approaching enemy with Thresh E Flay and shield your carry with Thresh W Dark Passage. New crowd control still affects Alistar after he activates his ultimate, so if you can’t back away, stop his engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence or Thresh E Flay.
Alistar.laning: Take control of the brush and look for an angle to use Thresh Q Death Sentence when Alistar is busy last-hitting or casting an ability. If it’s hard to hold the brush, fall back, protect your carry’s CS, and collect souls. Don’t risk walking into the enemy’s range for a soul; collect it with Thresh W Dark Passage or leave it.
Alistar.build: Alistar’s main damage is magic, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so buy a Null-Magic Mantle first. Choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. If the healing from Alistar P Triumphant Roar can prolong fights, get an Oblivion Orb for Grievous Wounds.
Alistar.combo: If Alistar is close, use Thresh E Flay to pull him and disrupt his movement, then throw Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Thresh Q Death Sentence hits first, auto attack, then use Thresh E Flay as the stun ends to pull him toward your allies. If needed, block his escape with Thresh R The Box. Recasting Thresh Q Death Sentence sends Thresh flying in, so only do it when your allies can follow.
Alistar.escape: If Alistar Q Pulverize is down too, engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence or bring an ally in with Thresh W Dark Passage. Then use Thresh E Flay to keep the enemy in place.
Alistar.fight: Fight back right after Alistar W Headbutt and Alistar Q Pulverize are down. Against an Alistar who is already close, use Thresh E Flay to pull him first, then throw Thresh Q Death Sentence. When Alistar R Unbreakable Will is active, don’t spend your damage on him; back off and fight again after it ends.
Alistar.watch: Alistar W Headbutt is a displacement and a dash, while Alistar Q Pulverize knocks you up, so watch for the two abilities used together. Near a turret, don’t give Alistar room to circle behind you. Watch your spacing so you don’t get caught by the stun from Alistar E Trample, either.

Swain.combo: After Swain E Nevermove is used, hit Thresh Q Death Sentence, land one basic attack, then pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. As the stun from Thresh Q Death Sentence is about to end, follow with Thresh E Flay. Use Thresh R The Box to block his escape direction if needed. Don't recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to fly in if your allies can't follow from that position.
Swain.build: Swain deals mostly magic damage, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If Swain's healing prolongs fights, get healing reduction with Oblivion Orb. If Swain can root and pick off your carry, include Mikael's Blessing in your core build.
Swain.escape: Swain has no mobility or escape ability, so look to engage immediately after Swain E Nevermove has been spent. Make sure the returning wave has disappeared, then catch him with Thresh Q Death Sentence. If your allies can follow, help them join with Thresh W Dark Passage. Then hold Swain toward your allies with Thresh E Flay.
Swain.fight: After dodging the returning wave from Swain E Nevermove, engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence while Swain can't cast E again. If you're already close, pull him first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence. Don't let a fight drag on beside Swain while R Demonic Ascension is active.
Swain.laning: Dodge the outgoing and returning paths of Swain E Nevermove, and keep your distance so Swain Q Death's Hand doesn't hit you with overlapping bolts. If collecting a soul would put you in danger, retrieve it with Thresh W Dark Passage or give it up.
Swain.phase: Early on, Thresh can take lane control before Swain builds growth stacks and limit his chance to scale. From mid game onward, the outcome of the same engage depends on how many stacks Swain has, so choose an opening after Swain E Nevermove is used. In late game, watch out for Swain's permanent scaling and healing from Swain R Demonic Ascension. Get healing reduction and create distance when his ultimate is active.
Swain.teamfight: When Swain R Demonic Ascension is active, back out of range with your allies and re-engage after it ends. If Swain E Nevermove roots your carry, help them escape with Thresh W Dark Passage and its shield, but Thresh W Dark Passage and Thresh E Flay can't remove an immobilizing effect that's already applied, so use Mikael's Blessing. When retreating, place Thresh R The Box along the chase route so Swain is slowed as he passes through a wall.
Swain.watch: Swain E Nevermove also roots on the returning wave, so stay out of its path until it fully disappears. Swain Q Death's Hand hits with several bolts overlapping at close range, so keep your distance. When Swain R Demonic Ascension is active, it drains nearby enemies and heals him, so get out of range and wait for his ultimate to end.

Brand.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Brand’s main damage is magic, so building magic resistance first is effective for Thresh.
Brand.combo: After Brand W Pillar of Flame is down, land Thresh Q Death Sentence, get one auto attack in, then pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block Brand’s escape direction. If you’re already close, disrupt his movement first with Thresh E Flay, then throw Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Brand.escape: Brand has no mobility, so engage when Brand W Pillar of Flame is down and he remains within range. If you’re ablaze, dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear before engaging. Even if Thresh Q Death Sentence hits, don’t recast it to fly in from a position your allies can’t follow.
Brand.fight: Look for an engage when Brand W Pillar of Flame is down. Throw Thresh Q Death Sentence when Brand is locked into casting an ability or from an angle without vision. If you get close, pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. If you’re ablaze, dodge the stun from Brand Q Sear before moving in.
Brand.laning: Take control of the brush to create an angle for a hidden Thresh Q Death Sentence, and fall back to protect your carry’s CS if the brush is contested. Don’t stand beside burning minions, and step to the side when the wave is grouped together. Collect souls within the enemy’s range with Thresh W Dark Passage or leave them.
Brand.phase: Early on, Thresh can start fights with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing Brand out of lane and collecting souls instead of fixating on kills. In the mid game, pick up souls as you pass through fight locations and around jungle camps. Thresh’s late game durability depends on the number of souls collected, so the information provided isn’t enough to say which side is stronger.
Brand.teamfight: Spread out from your allies to reduce the spread of Brand E Conflagration and the bounces from Brand R Pyroclasm, and don’t stand beside an ally who is ablaze. If your team needs protection, hold Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel off nearby enemies with Thresh E Flay, and shield your allies with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, target Brand with Thresh Q Death Sentence and block his escape direction with Thresh R The Box.
Brand.watch: Brand P Blaze stacks when you’re hit by abilities in quick succession, then explodes, so it’s important to dodge the first ability, Brand W Pillar of Flame or Brand Q Sear. While ablaze, getting hit by Brand Q Sear stuns you, so get out of its projectile path or hide behind a minion. Watch for Brand E Conflagration spreading near burning minions, and move away from allies when Brand R Pyroclasm appears.

Braum.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first to withstand Braum’s magic damage. Choose Mercury’s Treads for boots.
Braum.combo: After Braum W Stand Behind Me is down, land Thresh Q Death Sentence from an angle outside the front of his shield, get one auto attack in, then pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Only recast Thresh Q Death Sentence when your allies can follow.
Braum.escape: The moment after Braum W Stand Behind Me is down is your window to close the gap and pick him off. Engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence and follow with Thresh E Flay, but don’t recast Thresh Q Death Sentence from a position your allies can’t follow.
Braum.fight: Gauge your distance from behind minions so you can dodge Braum Q Winter’s Bite, then look to engage right after Braum W Stand Behind Me is down. If you get close, first pull him with Thresh E Flay to disrupt his movement, then land Thresh Q Death Sentence. For trades, wait, then combine one empowered auto attack with Thresh E Flay.
Braum.laning: Take control of the brush and look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from an angle Braum can’t see. Braum Q Winter’s Bite only hits the first target, so stand behind minions, and don’t stand directly in line with Braum when there’s a gap between minions. Instead of walking into danger to collect a soul, use Thresh W Dark Passage or leave it.
Braum.phase: Early on, Thresh can create a kill opportunity with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but the goal is to push the enemy out of lane and collect souls rather than force a kill. Keep picking up souls around fight locations and jungle camps in the mid game. Thresh’s late game durability depends on the souls collected, so base your fight on how many souls you’ve stacked and the engage setup rather than assuming one side is stronger.
Braum.teamfight: If your team is fighting from the back, hold Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, avoid the front of Braum E Unbreakable and target the back line Braum is protecting with Thresh Q Death Sentence. Move to the side to get out of the line of Braum R Glacial Fissure, and block the path with Thresh R The Box when you’re being chased.
Braum.watch: If Braum Q Winter’s Bite or Braum P Concussive Blows marks you, get out of range before the stacks fill. Projectiles are blocked in front of Braum while Braum E Unbreakable is active, so wait for the shield to drop or find an angle from the side. Watch the cast animation for Braum R Glacial Fissure and dodge sideways; don’t step into the slow zone it leaves behind, either.

Heimerdinger.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Heimerdinger’s main damage is magic, so build magic resistance first.
Heimerdinger.combo: After landing Thresh Q Death Sentence from the brush, get one auto attack in, then pull Heimerdinger toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block his escape. Only recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to go in when your allies can follow immediately, and help them engage with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Heimerdinger.escape: Close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence or bring an ally in with Thresh W Dark Passage, then hold Heimerdinger with Thresh E Flay. If your allies can’t follow, don’t recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to go deep, even if it hits.
Heimerdinger.fight: Don’t keep trading head-on in front of Heimerdinger’s turrets; target Heimerdinger from the brush or the side. Once you’re close, make a short trade with one saved auto attack and Thresh E Flay.
Heimerdinger.laning: Take control of the brush first, then look for an angle for Thresh Q Death Sentence while Heimerdinger is last-hitting or using an ability. If it’s hard to hold the brush, fall back, protect your carry’s CS, and collect souls. Don’t risk walking for a soul within the enemy’s range; collect it with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Heimerdinger.phase: Early on, Thresh can start a fight with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but avoid trading in front of Heimerdinger’s fully charged turrets. Thresh’s durability in the late game depends on the souls collected, so keep gathering souls after laning phase.
Heimerdinger.teamfight: If your team is fighting from the back, hold Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, target Heimerdinger himself from the side and block his escape with Thresh R The Box. When Heimerdinger R UPGRADE!!! is ready, don’t group together in a narrow area in front of an objective.
Heimerdinger.watch: When you see the landing indicator, move sideways to avoid the center. If you’re hit, get out of turret range.

Hwei.build: Early on, buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury’s Treads for boots. Hwei’s main damage is magic, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If immobilizing crowd control from Hwei E Subject: Torment leaves your carry caught and vulnerable to being killed, include Mikael’s Blessing in your core build.
Hwei.combo: Against a nearby Hwei, pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay, then land Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Thresh Q Death Sentence hits first from the brush, weave in auto attacks, then pull him again with Thresh E Flay as the stun ends to continue immobilizing him. Only recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to go in when your allies can follow, and if needed, block his escape direction with Thresh R The Box.
Hwei.escape: Hwei has no mobility, so the moment after Hwei E Subject: Torment is down is your chance to engage. Close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence and hold him with Thresh E Flay; if your allies can join, bring them in with Thresh W Dark Passage. If Hwei E Subject: Torment is still available, he can root or push you back at the front of the engage, so wait until you see him use it.
Hwei.fight: Close the gap right after Hwei E Subject: Torment is used for poke or wave clear. If you get close, pull him first with Thresh E Flay, then throw Thresh Q Death Sentence, weaving in auto attacks one at a time that you have saved until just before the trade. If Hwei’s first ability has hit you, move to avoid follow-up abilities instead of continuing the trade.
Hwei.laning: Take control of the brush first, then look for an angle for Thresh Q Death Sentence when Hwei is last-hitting or using an ability. If the brush is contested, fall back and protect your carry’s CS. Collect souls in dangerous spots with Thresh W Dark Passage or leave them. Before calling for a gank, check whether Hwei E Subject: Torment has left an eye behind.
Hwei.phase: Early on, Thresh can create an opportunity with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing Hwei out of lane and collecting souls instead of forcing a kill. In the mid game, Hwei can narrow paths with ground effects and eyes, so take a wide route around the affected areas. In the late game, the souls collected with Thresh P Damnation affect his durability, so keep collecting them around fight locations and jungle camps.
Hwei.teamfight: If your team is fighting from the back, hold Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel off an approaching enemy with Thresh E Flay, and protect your allies with the shield from Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, target Hwei with Thresh Q Death Sentence after Hwei E Subject: Torment is down, and only recast it to go in when your allies can follow. Place Thresh R The Box in Hwei’s escape direction, or along the path a pursuer must take when you’re retreating.
Hwei.watch: If you’re hit by Hwei E Subject: Torment’s root or displacement, you’re likely to get hit by follow-up attacks, so don’t go in first while the Torment subject is still available. If Hwei’s first ability hits you, move immediately to avoid his second ability and the explosion from Hwei P Signature of the Visionary. Hwei Q Subject: Disaster can deal damage based on your maximum or missing health, so leave the marked area and ground effect.

Janna.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots early. Janna deals mostly magic damage, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so prioritize magic resistance. If the healing from Janna R Monsoon can prolong a fight, get an Oblivion Orb to reduce healing.
Janna.combo: If Janna is close, pull her in first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence. If you land Thresh Q Death Sentence from brush, follow with a basic attack, then use Thresh E Flay toward your allies as the stun wears off. Recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to go in only when your allies can follow, and use Thresh R The Box to block her escape route.
Janna.escape: A Janna Q Howling Gale miss is an opportunity to close the gap with Thresh Q Death Sentence. Once Janna R Monsoon is down, she has one less way to knock away an engage, so check whether your allies can follow before going in. If Janna W Zephyr is still available to slow you, look for an angle from brush instead of walking straight at her.
Janna.fight: Bait out Janna E Eye Of The Storm, then target someone without a shield. After Janna uses Q Howling Gale or R Monsoon, look for an angle from brush or outside vision to engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence. At close range, trade briefly with a saved basic attack and Thresh E Flay.
Janna.laning: Secure brush vision first, then pressure the ally Janna is protecting to make her use E Eye Of The Storm. You can strain her mana by making her waste Q Howling Gale and W Zephyr. Instead of forcing a kill, push the opponent out of lane and collect souls with Thresh P Damnation; use Thresh W Dark Passage to collect souls in dangerous positions.
Janna.phase: Early on, you can start a fight with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on lane pressure and collecting souls rather than forcing a kill. Keep collecting souls with Thresh P Damnation around fights and jungle camps as the game progresses. In late-game team fights, Janna R Monsoon can knock away an engage, so choose whether to engage or peel based on how your allies are entering the fight.
Janna.teamfight: If Janna is protecting from behind an allied carry, secure vision and look for an isolated Janna with Thresh Q Death Sentence. If your team is fighting from behind, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off with Thresh E Flay, and protect your allies with Thresh W Dark Passage. When your allies engage first, go in from a distance they can follow and use Thresh R The Box to block the enemy’s path.
Janna.watch: If you hear Janna Q Howling Gale from outside your vision, move out of the tornado’s path. A target protected by Janna E Eye Of The Storm has a shield and can trade back more effectively, so don’t commit your damage during that window. Janna R Monsoon knocks away Thresh when he engages and heals nearby allies, so check whether it has been used before going in.

Karma.build: Karma deals mostly magic damage, so build a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads. If the healing from Karma’s empowered W with R Mantra prolongs fights, get an Oblivion Orb early.
Karma.combo: If Karma W Focused Resolve is down, combo Thresh Q Death Sentence hit → basic attack → Thresh E Flay to pull her toward your allies. If Karma is close, pull her in first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence. Follow with Thresh R The Box when you need to block her escape route, and recast Q only when your allies can follow.
Karma.escape: Karma has no mobility ability to create distance herself, but Karma E Inspire can increase her movement speed. Bait out Karma W Focused Resolve, then engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence during the window after the shield from her empowered E with R Mantra ends.
Karma.fight: Engage after Karma W Focused Resolve is down and the shield from her empowered E with R Mantra has ended. Look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from brush or an angle outside vision; at close range, pull her in first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Q. Save your basic attack until just before trading to make use of Thresh E Flay’s passive.
Karma.laning: The more Karma hits you with abilities, the more Karma P Gathering Fire reduces the cooldown of R Mantra, so dodge her poke by moving behind minions or out of range. Secure brush vision to create an angle for Thresh Q Death Sentence. If you can’t hold the brush, protect your carry’s CS and collect souls with Thresh P Damnation. Use Thresh W Dark Passage to collect souls in dangerous positions, and give them up if needed.
Karma.teamfight: While Karma W Focused Resolve is available, only the ally who engages first may get rooted, so bait it out before starting the fight. If Karma’s empowered E with R Mantra shields nearby allies, hold off on a burst engage until the shield expires. When you need to protect your allies, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off with Thresh E Flay, and provide a shield and escape route with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Karma.watch: Karma Q Inner Flame applies an area slow, and the empowered Q from Karma R Mantra creates a burning area that detonates again after a short delay. If hit, leave the area immediately. If Karma W Focused Resolve connects, create distance before the root takes hold, and look for an angle to knock Karma away with Thresh E Flay.

Leona.build: Build a Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Leona deals mostly magic damage, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. After that, choose resistances based on the damage type of the enemy carry dealing damage while Leona holds a target in place.
Leona.combo: If Leona E Zenith Blade is down and you can get close, pull her toward your allies with Thresh E Flay, then land Thresh Q Death Sentence. If you land Thresh Q Death Sentence first, follow with Thresh E Flay as the stun wears off, and use Thresh R The Box to block her escape route if needed. Recast Thresh Q Death Sentence only when your allies can follow.
Leona.escape: The moment Leona E Zenith Blade, her mobility tool, is down is your window to close the gap. Look for Thresh Q Death Sentence or use Thresh W Dark Passage to bring an ally in, then follow up on the target you reach with Thresh E Flay. If Leona Q Shield of Daybreak and R Solar Flare’s crowd control are still available, account for that danger before engaging.
Leona.fight: Don’t take extended physical damage trades against Leona’s high early-game defenses. After Leona E Zenith Blade is down, trade briefly with a saved basic attack and Thresh E Flay. If Leona W Eclipse is active, leave its area to avoid the explosion, then look for another angle.
Leona.laning: Secure brush vision and look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from an unseen angle. If you lose the brush, protect your carry’s CS and collect souls. Don’t stand in a line with your carry where Leona E Zenith Blade can reach both of you. Use Thresh W Dark Passage to collect souls in dangerous positions instead of walking forward to pick them up.
Leona.phase: In the mid game, close the gap aggressively only in the moment after Leona E Zenith Blade is used, and keep collecting souls. In the late game, Thresh’s armor and ability power scale with the souls he has collected, so pick up souls around fights and jungle camps too.
Leona.teamfight: If you need to protect your carry, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel Leona off with Thresh E Flay, and protect your ally with Thresh W Dark Passage. Thresh W Dark Passage and E Flay can’t remove an immobilizing effect that has already landed, so if the enemy composition can lock down and kill your carry, build Mikael's Blessing as a core item. If Leona P Sunlight is applied, watch for follow-up damage and back away. Use Thresh R The Box on the escape route when you need to stop a chase.
Leona.watch: Leona E Zenith Blade pierces in a straight line and attaches to the last champion hit, so don’t stand in a line with your carry. Leona can activate Q Shield of Daybreak before approaching, so watch the distance rather than whether she has used the ability. When Leona W Eclipse is active, leave its area before it explodes. When Leona R Solar Flare’s indicator appears, move sideways to avoid the center stun.

Lulu.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots early. Lulu deals mostly magic damage, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. After that, choose resistances based on the damage type of the target Lulu is protecting.
Lulu.combo: If Lulu W Whimsy is down and your allies can follow, fight with Thresh Q Death Sentence hit → basic attack → Thresh E Flay to pull her toward your allies. Use Thresh R The Box to block Lulu’s escape route if needed. If Lulu is close, disrupt her first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Lulu.escape: Lulu has no dash to disengage, so the window to engage is after Lulu W Whimsy is used on another ally. Close the gap with Thresh Q Death Sentence and use Thresh E Flay to pull Lulu toward your allies and hold her there. If Lulu R Wild Growth is still available, account for the possibility that it can save its target when choosing whom to engage on.
Lulu.fight: Don’t dive deep while Lulu W Whimsy is available; poke with a saved Thresh E Flay and one basic attack. When Lulu uses W on another ally and gives a shield and Pix to her carry, target Lulu herself. Even if you land Thresh Q Death Sentence, don’t recast it if your allies can’t follow.
Lulu.laning: Stand behind minions to reduce the bonus damage from Lulu P Pix, Faerie Companion. Secure brush vision and look for an angle for Thresh Q Death Sentence when Lulu is occupied with a last hit or casting an ability. Poke steadily and collect souls instead of relying on one big engage; use Thresh W Dark Passage to collect souls that drop in dangerous positions.
Lulu.phase: In the mid game, look for opportunities after Lulu uses her protective abilities, and keep collecting souls instead of forcing an engage. Thresh’s late-game durability depends on the souls he has collected, and avoid fights that rely on killing a target with Lulu R Wild Growth still available in one burst.
Lulu.teamfight: If you need to protect your allies, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, knock enemies off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies can engage first, target someone in the back line with Thresh Q Death Sentence while Lulu W Whimsy is down. If Lulu R Wild Growth is still available, target Lulu herself or someone else instead of the ally it can protect.
Lulu.watch: Lulu W Whimsy can stop Thresh’s engage, so save the recast of Thresh Q Death Sentence until Lulu uses W on another ally. Lulu R Wild Growth can knock up nearby enemies and save its target, so don’t dive deep for what looks like a guaranteed kill while it’s available. Watch out for the slow from Lulu Q Glitterlance too, and walk out of the areas she lays down to push.

Lux.build: Build a Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Lux deals mostly magic damage, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If the enemy composition relies on Lux Q Light Binding to catch and kill your carry, build Mikael's Blessing as a core item.
Lux.combo: After Lux Q Light Binding misses, land Thresh Q Death Sentence, basic attack, then use Thresh E Flay to pull her toward your allies. If you’re already close, pull her in first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence at close range.
Lux.escape: A Lux Q Light Binding miss is your chance to engage. Lux has no mobility ability, so close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence and stop her movement with Thresh E Flay, but recast Thresh Q Death Sentence only when your allies can follow.
Lux.fight: Bait out Lux Q Light Binding and dodge it, then approach from brush or the side. Lux has no mobility ability, so once you close the gap, disrupt her with Thresh E Flay and trade with a saved empowered basic attack. Even if you land Thresh Q Death Sentence, don’t recast it to go in if your allies can’t follow from that position.
Lux.laning: Spread out to the side from your allies so Lux Q Light Binding doesn’t catch you all together. Secure brush vision and look for Thresh Q Death Sentence when Lux is occupied with a last hit or casting an ability. If the brush is being poked, back off and protect your carry’s CS. Use Thresh W Dark Passage to collect souls that drop in dangerous positions or give them up.
Lux.phase: Early on, Thresh can create kill opportunities with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing the enemy out of lane and collecting souls rather than forcing a kill. Keep picking up souls around fights and jungle camps in the mid game. Thresh’s late-game durability depends on how many souls he has collected; the available information isn’t enough to say which side is stronger.
Lux.teamfight: Approach from a different direction than your allies so Lux E Lucent Singularity doesn’t catch you all together. When you need to protect your allies, peel enemies off with Thresh E Flay and shield them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies can engage first, target Lux with Thresh Q Death Sentence after Lux Q Light Binding is down, and block her escape route with Thresh R The Box.
Lux.watch: Lux Q Light Binding roots up to the first two enemies it hits, so don’t stand in a line with your ally. If it hits, Lux’s follow-up abilities are hard to avoid, so engage after it misses. Leave the area affected by Lux E Lucent Singularity, and sidestep when you see the aim line for Lux R Final Spark.

Maokai.build: Maokai deals mostly magic damage, so buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots early. After that, choose resistances based on the enemy carry dealing damage while Maokai holds a target in place. If the enemy composition can lock down and kill your carry, build Mikael's Blessing as a core item.
Maokai.combo: After Maokai W Twisted Advance is down, land Thresh Q Death Sentence, basic attack once, then use Thresh E Flay to pull him toward your allies. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block his escape route. Recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to go in deep only if your allies can follow and you can bring them in with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Maokai.escape: Maokai W Twisted Advance is his only mobility tool, so immediately after forcing him to use it is your chance to engage. Close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence or bring in an ally with Thresh W Dark Passage, then use Thresh E Flay on Maokai after he lands to keep him from getting away.
Maokai.fight: Move forward and trade immediately after forcing Maokai to use W Twisted Advance. Focus ability poke on the enemy carry so Maokai P Sap Magic doesn’t get to heal often.
Maokai.laning: Don’t enter brush where Maokai E Sapling Toss has been planted. If you have vision in safe brush, look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from an unseen angle. If the brush is contested, back off, protect your carry’s CS, and collect souls. Use Thresh W Dark Passage to collect souls that drop within enemy range, or give them up.
Maokai.teamfight: If your allies are fighting from behind, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel Maokai off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and protect your ally with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, use Thresh Q Death Sentence to target the enemy back line. Avoid narrow passages where Maokai R Nature's Grasp is approaching, and fight in open terrain.
Maokai.watch: Maokai W Twisted Advance dashes in and roots you, so don’t enter its range near brush while it’s available. Avoid brush where Maokai E Sapling Toss has been planted, and if a sapling follows you, lead it toward minions or monsters rather than your allies. Maokai R Nature's Grasp can root you for a long time from a distance, so move perpendicular to its path.

Milio.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots early. Milio deals magic damage, but also account for the enemy carry’s damage type when choosing later resistances. If Milio W Cozy Campfire and R Breath of Life prolong fights, get an Oblivion Orb to reduce healing.
Milio.combo: At close range, pull Milio toward your allies with Thresh E Flay, then land Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Q hits first, basic attack, then use E toward your allies as the stun wears off to continue the crowd control. Recast Q to engage only when your allies can follow, and use Thresh R The Box to block his escape route if needed.
Milio.escape: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick being down is your window to engage. Look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from brush or an angle outside vision, then pull Milio toward your allies with Thresh E Flay once you’re close. Even if Q hits, don’t recast it to fly in if your allies can’t follow from that position.
Milio.fight: Look for a chance to get on Milio after Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick is down. Instead of throwing Thresh Q Death Sentence first from open ground, look for an angle from brush, or disrupt him with Thresh E Flay at close range before casting Q. When trading, use one saved basic attack together with E.
Milio.laning: Early on, pressure Milio’s mana through attrition and take control of the wave. Secure brush vision first to create an angle for Thresh Q Death Sentence; if there’s no angle, protect your carry’s CS and collect souls. Use Thresh W Dark Passage to collect souls within enemy range, or give them up if the lane state is unfavorable.
Milio.phase: Early on, you can start a fight with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing Milio out of lane and collecting souls rather than forcing a kill. Keep collecting souls around fights and jungle camps in the mid game. Milio’s team gets stronger as the game goes on, so pressure him during the laning phase through attrition and control of the wave.
Milio.teamfight: If your allies are fighting from behind, save Q, peel enemies off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and withstand the fight with the shield from Thresh W Dark Passage. Place Thresh R The Box on escape routes or chase paths the enemy has to cross.
Milio.watch: Milio Q Ultra Mega Fire Kick knocks back the first enemy it hits, so it’s the ability Thresh needs to watch most when engaging. Hold off on fighting the front line while Milio W Cozy Campfire extends the enemy ranged carry’s range. Milio R Breath of Life heals and grants tenacity, so don’t dive deep right after it’s used based only on a crowd-control combo.

Morgana.build: Build a Null-Magic Mantle early to survive, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Morgana deals mostly magic damage, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If your carry can be caught and killed while rooted, build Mikael's Blessing as a core item. If Morgana’s healing prolongs fights, buy an Oblivion Orb.
Morgana.combo: After Morgana E Black Shield is down, land Thresh Q Death Sentence, basic attack, then use Thresh E Flay to pull her toward your allies. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block her escape route. Recast Thresh Q Death Sentence only when your allies can follow.
Morgana.escape: The window after Morgana E Black Shield is down is your chance to apply crowd control and engage. Morgana has no ability to create distance on her own, so close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence and hold her with E Flay. If there’s no angle to dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding, delay your engage.
Morgana.fight: Don’t waste the crowd control from Thresh Q Death Sentence or E Flay on a target protected by Morgana E Black Shield. After the shield is down, look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from brush or an angle outside vision. At close range, disrupt the target first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence. Save your basic attacks until just before a fight, and attack one at a time.
Morgana.laning: Stay in line with minions to dodge Morgana Q Dark Binding while securing brush vision. Look for Thresh Q Death Sentence when Morgana is occupied with a last hit or casting an ability. Keep collecting souls, but use Thresh W Dark Passage to collect them or give them up if they drop within enemy range.
Morgana.teamfight: If your allies are fighting from behind, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off your carry with E Flay, and protect them with W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, target an enemy in the back line with Thresh Q Death Sentence while Morgana E Black Shield is down. Thresh W Dark Passage and E Flay can’t free an ally who has already been hit by Morgana Q Dark Binding, so use Mikael's Blessing to cover that weakness in such situations.
Morgana.watch: Morgana Q Dark Binding only roots the first target it hits, so dodge it by keeping minions between you and Morgana. Morgana R Soul Shackles stuns after a delay, so when you see the tether, use Thresh Q Death Sentence or W Dark Passage to get out of range.

Nami.build: Survive early with a Null-Magic Mantle, and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Most of Nami’s damage is magic, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If Nami W Ebb and Flow’s healing prolongs fights, get an Oblivion Orb for Grievous Wounds.
Nami.combo: If you’re close to Nami, pull her toward your allies with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Q hits first, auto-attack, then pull her toward your allies again with E as the stun is about to end. Follow up with Thresh R The Box when you need to block her escape route, and recast Q only when your allies can follow up.
Nami.escape: Nami has no mobility spell, so the moment Nami Q Aqua Prison misses is your chance to close the distance. If you see Nami R Tidal Wave, sidestep first, watch for the Q that follows, then engage. If your allies can follow, recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to go in after it hits, then follow up with Thresh E Flay.
Nami.fight: Target Nami right after Nami Q Aqua Prison misses. Cast Thresh Q Death Sentence from a brush or an angle without vision; if you’re already close, pull her in first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Q. Delay the fight while Nami E Tidecaller's Blessing is active.
Nami.laning: Secure brush vision first to create an angle where Nami has trouble seeing Thresh Q Death Sentence. If you lose the brush, don’t walk in recklessly; protect your allied marksman’s CS and collect souls. Retrieve souls that fall within Nami’s range with Thresh W Dark Passage, and give them up if it’s dangerous.
Nami.phase: In lane, focus on pushing Nami out of lane and stacking souls rather than forcing a kill. Keep collecting souls around skirmishes and jungle camps in the mid and late game to keep Thresh P Damnation scaling.
Nami.teamfight: If your allies are playing back, save Thresh Q Death Sentence and use Thresh E Flay to peel enemies off your allied damage dealers. When allies are in danger after Nami Q Aqua Prison or Nami R Tidal Wave, use Thresh W Dark Passage to give them a shield and an escape route. If your allies engage first, target the enemy backline with Q and block their escape direction with Thresh R The Box.
Nami.watch: Nami Q Aqua Prison falls slowly, but stuns if it hits, so sidestep when you see it coming. Nami R Tidal Wave travels from far away, but moves slowly enough that you can sidestep as soon as you see it. Don’t fight head-on against a target affected by Nami E Tidecaller's Blessing; reengage after it expires.

Nautilus.build: Nautilus’s main damage is magic, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Buy a Null-Magic Mantle early and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If Nautilus is part of a composition that locks down and takes out your allied damage dealers, build Mikael's Blessing as a core item.
Nautilus.combo: If Nautilus Q Dredge Line is down and your allies can follow, fight in this order: hit Thresh Q Death Sentence → auto-attack → pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. If Nautilus is already close, pull him first with Thresh E Flay and cast Thresh Q Death Sentence at point-blank range. Recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to fly in only when the engage is certain, and block his escape route with Thresh R The Box.
Nautilus.escape: The moment Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses is your window to engage. He has no other way to move using terrain, so close the distance with Thresh Q Death Sentence or Thresh W Dark Passage at that moment, then follow up with Thresh E Flay. If your allies can’t follow, don’t recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to go deep, even if it hits.
Nautilus.fight: Right after Nautilus Q Dredge Line misses, close the distance with Thresh Q Death Sentence or Thresh W Dark Passage and catch him with Thresh E Flay. Cast Thresh Q Death Sentence from a brush or an angle without vision; if you’re already close, disrupt his movement first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Q. During a damage trade, pair Thresh E Flay’s poke with an auto-attack you’ve held back.
Nautilus.laning: Stand with minions between you and Nautilus Q Dredge Line while securing brush vision. If you give up the brush, protect your allied damage dealer’s CS and collect souls instead of recklessly casting Thresh Q Death Sentence. Retrieve souls within Nautilus’s range with Thresh W Dark Passage, or give them up.
Nautilus.phase: Early on, Thresh can start fights with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but Nautilus Q Dredge Line is also a key skill for setting up kills, so watch for it to go down first. In the mid game, keep collecting souls around skirmishes and jungle camps. Thresh’s late-game durability depends on how many souls he has collected, so keep gathering souls and decide each fight whether to protect your allies or engage.
Nautilus.teamfight: If your allies are playing back, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, push an engaging Nautilus away from your damage dealers with Thresh E Flay, and shield them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, target the enemy backline with Thresh Q Death Sentence while Nautilus Q Dredge Line is down. Position so your allies don’t overlap along the path of Nautilus R Depth Charge while it’s available.
Nautilus.watch: Nautilus Q Dredge Line is his main engage tool, so avoid it by keeping minions between you. Nautilus P Staggering Blow roots you on his first basic attack, so don’t hesitate within his attack range. Nautilus R Depth Charge follows its target and knocks up allies along its path, so don’t stand on top of each other while his ultimate is available.

Neeko.build: Survive early with a Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads. Neeko’s main damage is magic, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If the enemy can root you with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs and then kill you with Neeko R Pop Blossom, prioritize tenacity.
Neeko.combo: If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is down and your allies can follow, hit Thresh Q Death Sentence, auto-attack, then pull her toward your allies with Thresh E Flay as the stun ends. At close range, pull her first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence. Follow up with Thresh R The Box if you need to block Neeko’s escape direction.
Neeko.escape: If Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is also down, close the distance with Thresh Q Death Sentence and Thresh W Dark Passage, then catch her with Thresh E Flay. Even if Thresh Q Death Sentence hits, don’t recast it if your allies can’t follow from that position.
Neeko.fight: The moment Neeko E Tangle-Barbs is down is your chance to trade. Poke with an auto-attack you’ve held back and Thresh E Flay, and engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence when your allies can follow. Thresh’s damage is mostly magic, and Neeko has relatively low magic resistance.
Neeko.laning: Secure brush vision first, then look for Thresh Q Death Sentence when Neeko is last-hitting or casting a spell. Spread out so Neeko E Tangle-Barbs can’t root two allies at once, and walk out of the area hit by Neeko Q Blooming Burst. Retrieve souls that fall within enemy range with Thresh W Dark Passage, or give them up.
Neeko.phase: Once Neeko R Pop Blossom is available, watch for engages while transformed and fight while her ultimate is down. Thresh’s late-game durability depends on how many souls he has collected, so keep collecting souls around skirmishes and jungle camps after laning phase.
Neeko.teamfight: If an opponent you suspect is Neeko in disguise approaches, spread out from your allies so Neeko R Pop Blossom can’t hit you all together. When protecting an allied damage dealer, push an approaching Neeko away with Thresh E Flay and shield them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If the enemy composition can root and catch your allied damage dealer with Neeko E Tangle-Barbs, build Mikael's Blessing as a core item.
Neeko.watch: Neeko E Tangle-Barbs grows and speeds up if it hits something first, making it easier to root allies behind the first target, so spread out. If an opponent transformed by Neeko P Inherent Glamour approaches, Neeko R Pop Blossom’s windup may be hidden, so spread out in advance. Don’t attack the clone from Neeko W Shapesplitter; watch for the real Neeko’s position.

Pantheon.build: Pantheon’s main ability damage is physical, so build armor first. Pantheon W Shield Vault deals damage based on your maximum health, so avoid relying on a large health increase alone. Keep in mind that Pantheon R Grand Starfall’s armor penetration ignores some of your armor, even if you build it.
Pantheon.combo: If Pantheon W Shield Vault is down and your allies can follow, hit Thresh Q Death Sentence, auto-attack, then pull him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Place the walls of Thresh R The Box along Pantheon’s escape route. If Pantheon is already close, disrupt his movement first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Pantheon.escape: Pantheon W Shield Vault being down is your chance to engage, but Pantheon can use Pantheon R Grand Starfall to escape if it’s still available. In particular, before Pantheon R Grand Starfall comes back up, close the distance with Thresh Q Death Sentence and bring your allies in with Thresh W Dark Passage. Then catch Pantheon with Thresh E Flay.
Pantheon.fight: Avoid trading blow for blow while Pantheon is strong early, and make short trades with Thresh E Flay and an auto-attack you’ve held back. When Pantheon E Aegis Assault is active, don’t try to damage him from the front; wait for it to end. Once Pantheon W Shield Vault is down, look for an opening to engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Pantheon.laning: Secure brush vision and look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from an angle where you can’t be seen. When Pantheon Q Comet Spear is used to poke, keep minions between you and him, and don’t walk into Pantheon W Shield Vault range to collect souls. Retrieve souls in dangerous places with Thresh W Dark Passage or give them up; early on, focus on collecting souls safely and protecting your allied damage dealer’s CS rather than getting kills.
Pantheon.phase: In the mid game, start fights based on whether Pantheon W Shield Vault and Pantheon R Grand Starfall have been used. In the late game, Pantheon’s influence falls off while Thresh gains armor and ability power by consistently collecting souls, so let time work in Thresh’s favor.
Pantheon.teamfight: If your allies are playing back, save Thresh Q Death Sentence and push an engaging Pantheon away from your allied damage dealers with Thresh E Flay. Just before Pantheon’s burst damage lands, cast Thresh W Dark Passage to provide a shield and an escape route. If your allies engage first and Pantheon’s mobility options are down, catch him with Thresh Q Death Sentence and block his escape route with Thresh R The Box.
Pantheon.watch: Pantheon W Shield Vault stuns a targeted enemy, so don’t give him the range to use it. When Pantheon Q Comet Spear is used to poke, keep minions between you and him. If you see the landing warning for Pantheon R Grand Starfall, walk outside its landing area. Pantheon E Aegis Assault blocks damage from the direction he faces, so wait until it ends before attacking from the front.

Pyke.build: If Pyke P Gift of the Drowned Ones’ healing prolongs fights, buy an Oblivion Orb first for Grievous Wounds. Build armor rather than magic resistance against Pyke’s damage, and maintain enough health to stay above his execute threshold. Consistently collecting souls from Thresh P Damnation also increases your armor.
Pyke.combo: If you’ve dodged Pyke E Phantom Undertow and closed the distance, pull Pyke toward your allies with Thresh E Flay, then hit Thresh Q Death Sentence. Get one auto-attack in, and use Thresh R The Box to block Pyke’s escape direction if needed. If Thresh Q Death Sentence hits from far away first, follow up with Thresh E Flay as the stun ends.
Pyke.escape: The moment after dodging Pyke E Phantom Undertow is your chance to engage, but don’t go deep immediately if Pyke R Death From Below is still available. While Pyke R Death From Below is also down, close the distance with Thresh Q Death Sentence and cut off his escape route with Thresh E Flay. If your allies have difficulty joining you, don’t recast Thresh Q Death Sentence even if it hits.
Pyke.fight: After sidestepping the stun line from Pyke E Phantom Undertow, use Thresh E Flay on Pyke when he has a harder time escaping. If he’s already close, pull him first with Thresh E Flay, then follow up with Thresh Q Death Sentence. Before recasting Thresh Q Death Sentence to go in, check that your allies can follow from that position.
Pyke.laning: Secure brush vision first and look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from an angle Pyke has trouble seeing. Keep Pyke in vision as he retreats after a trade to prevent the healing from Pyke P Gift of the Drowned Ones. Retrieve souls in dangerous positions with Thresh W Dark Passage, and give them up if the lane state is bad.
Pyke.phase: Early on, Thresh can start fights with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing Pyke out of lane and stacking souls rather than getting kills. In the mid game, start fights while Pyke E Phantom Undertow and Pyke R Death From Below are down. In the late game, Thresh’s durability depends on how many souls he has collected, so keep collecting them and protect low-health allies who could be caught by Pyke R Death From Below.
Pyke.teamfight: If your allies are playing back, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, use Thresh E Flay to peel Pyke off your allied damage dealers, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. Low-health allies should spread out so they aren’t caught together by Pyke R Death From Below. If your allies engage first, catch one enemy with Thresh Q Death Sentence and block their escape direction with Thresh R The Box.
Pyke.watch: When you see the shark shadow from Pyke W Ghostwater Dive, move close to your allies. Dodge the stun from Pyke E Phantom Undertow by sidestepping the line it leaves behind. Keep your distance after being pulled by Pyke Q Bone Skewer, since Pyke E Phantom Undertow may follow. Watch for Pyke R Death From Below when your health is low, and don’t stand next to low-health allies.

Rakan.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Rakan’s damage is mostly magic, so prioritize magic resistance. If the healing from Rakan Q Gleaming Quill prolongs fights, get an Oblivion Orb for Grievous Wounds.
Rakan.combo: If Rakan gets close, pull him first with Thresh E Flay to disrupt his movement, then hit Thresh Q Death Sentence at point-blank range. Recast Q to follow him in only when your allies can engage with you.
Rakan.escape: The moment after you dodge or bait out Rakan W Grand Entrance is your chance to close the distance. Catch him with Thresh Q Death Sentence, then follow up with Thresh E Flay to limit his chance to escape. Rakan E Battle Dance can only target allied champions, so Rakan moving alone is also a good target.
Rakan.fight: Trade right after the shield from Rakan P Fey Feathers is removed. Dodge or bait out Rakan W Grand Entrance’s landing, then disrupt his movement with Thresh E Flay and cast Thresh Q Death Sentence at close range. Hold your auto-attack until just before the trade, then get one hit in.
Rakan.laning: Secure brush vision first and look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from an angle where you can’t be seen. If it’s hard to secure the brush, protect your allied damage dealer’s CS and collect souls. Retrieve souls that fall within Rakan’s threat range with Thresh W Dark Passage, or give them up.
Rakan.phase: Early on, Thresh can start fights with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing Rakan out of lane and stacking souls rather than forcing kills. Keep collecting souls around skirmishes and jungle camps after laning phase to build durability. In late-game teamfights, decide based on the fight whether to counter Rakan’s engage or help your allies engage.
Rakan.teamfight: If your allies are playing back, save Thresh Q Death Sentence and protect your allied damage dealers by pushing an engaging Rakan away with Thresh E Flay. Follow up with crowd control right after Rakan W Grand Entrance lands to stop his movement, and don’t line up with your allies before Rakan R The Quickness reaches you. If your allies engage first, catch the enemy backline with Thresh Q Death Sentence and create a path for your allies to follow with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Rakan.watch: Rakan W Grand Entrance has a visible landing point, so sidestep when Rakan starts moving to avoid the knockup. When Rakan R The Quickness is active, don’t line up with your allies, and push him away with Thresh E Flay before he reaches you.

Rell.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Rell’s damage is mostly magic, so compensate for Thresh’s low magic resistance first. Rell P Break the Mold reduces resistances, and Rell E Full Tilt deals damage based on maximum health, so don’t rely on a large health increase alone.
Rell.combo: If Rell gets close, disrupt her movement first with Thresh E Flay, then hit Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Thresh Q Death Sentence hits first, auto-attack, then pull her toward your allies with Thresh E Flay as the stun is about to end. Recast Thresh Q Death Sentence only when your allies can follow up, and use Thresh R The Box to block Rell’s escape direction if needed.
Rell.fight: Start trades outside Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down’s range, and back away when she rushes in with Rell E Full Tilt. After Rell engages with Crash Down, push her away with Thresh E Flay and create an escape route for your allies with Thresh W Dark Passage. Engage with Thresh Q Death Sentence once Rell’s mobility abilities are down and your allies can follow.
Rell.laning: Secure brush vision to create an angle where Rell has trouble seeing Thresh Q Death Sentence being cast. Rell has low magic resistance early and no way to heal in lane, so poke from outside Crash Down’s range and push her out of lane. Don’t walk in front of Rell to collect souls; retrieve souls in dangerous positions with Thresh W Dark Passage or give them up.
Rell.phase: The available information isn’t enough to determine who has the advantage in the mid or late game. Thresh should keep collecting souls around skirmishes and jungle camps after laning phase to build durability.
Rell.teamfight: Before a teamfight, spread out from your allies so Rell R Magnet Storm can’t pull several of you in together. If you’re protecting an allied damage dealer, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, push an engaging Rell away with Thresh E Flay, then use Thresh W Dark Passage’s shield once Rell Q Shattering Strike is down. If your allies engage first, target the enemy backline with Thresh Q Death Sentence and block their escape route with Thresh R The Box.
Rell.watch: If Rell and her ally both speed up with Rell E Full Tilt, it signals that she may jump in with Rell W Ferromancy: Crash Down, so stop trading and back out of its range. Rell Q Shattering Strike breaks shields, so sidestep it and use the shield from Thresh W Dark Passage after Rell Q Shattering Strike is down. In teamfights, keep your distance from allies so Rell R Magnet Storm can’t pull several of you in together.

Renata.build: Buy a Null-Magic Mantle first in the early game and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Prioritize magic resistance over armor against Renata Glasc’s damage. If Renata Glasc Q Handshake roots and catches your allied damage dealer, build Mikael's Blessing as a core item; if healing from Renata Glasc W Bailout prolongs fights, buy an Oblivion Orb first.
Renata.combo: After hitting Thresh Q Death Sentence, if your allies can follow, get one auto-attack in, then pull the enemy toward your allies with Thresh E Flay as they come out of the stun. Follow up with Thresh R The Box if you need to block their escape direction. To go deep, recast Thresh Q Death Sentence to engage, cast Thresh R The Box, then push with Thresh E Flay, but only try this when you can bring your allies in with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Renata.escape: If Renata Glasc Q Handshake misses or has been used, you have less reason to worry about being rooted, so look for an engage angle. Renata Glasc has no innate mobility spell, making her easy to catch with Thresh E Flay after you close the distance. If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is still available, engage with your allies spaced out so they don’t follow in a line.
Renata.fight: Look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from the brush when Renata Glasc is last-hitting or casting a spell. Even if it hits, don’t recast it to go in if your allies can’t follow. If she’s already close, pull her first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Renata.laning: Secure brush vision first and cast Thresh Q Death Sentence from an angle Renata Glasc can’t see. Renata Glasc has low health and attack damage early and no innate mobility spell, so pressure her directly when you can get close. If you lose the brush or a soul falls within enemy range, don’t walk in recklessly; retrieve the soul with Thresh W Dark Passage or give it up.
Renata.phase: Early on, Thresh can pressure Renata Glasc because of her low health and attack damage, but focus on pushing her out of lane and collecting souls rather than forcing a kill. Keep collecting souls around skirmishes and jungle camps in the mid game. In the late game, the souls Thresh has collected increase his armor and ability power, but the available information isn’t enough to determine which of the two champions is stronger.
Renata.teamfight: If Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available, engage with space between you and your allies. If your allies are playing back, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off your damage dealers with Thresh E Flay, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies have committed to an engage, target Renata Glasc with Thresh Q Death Sentence, then retreat immediately after killing an enemy affected by Renata Glasc W Bailout so your allies don’t die.
Renata.watch: If Renata Glasc Q Handshake hits you, you are rooted and can then be thrown, and allies at the landing spot can also be stunned. Stand behind minions or your frontline to avoid the initial hit, and sidestep Renata Glasc E Loyalty Program when it flies toward you. Keep your distance from allies while Renata Glasc R Hostile Takeover is available.

Senna.build: Senna's main damage is physical, so build armor first. If the healing from Senna Q Piercing Darkness can prolong fights, buy Oblivion Orb early. If the enemy composition can lock down and pick off your carries, include Mikael's Blessing in your core build.
Senna.combo: If Senna gets close, pull her toward your allies with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Q hits first from the brush, follow with a basic attack and pull her with E. Use Thresh R The Box to block her escape route when needed. Before recasting Q to go deep, make sure you can bring an ally with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Senna.escape: Look for an engage after Senna W Last Embrace misses and she steps forward to collect a soul. Senna has no ability to create distance on her own, so if Thresh Q Death Sentence closes the gap, hold her with Thresh E Flay. Throw Thresh W Dark Passage where an ally can join the fight.
Senna.fight: Trade when Senna steps forward to collect a soul. Save the empowered attack from Thresh E Flay to strike one hit at a time, then pull Senna closer with E and hit Thresh Q Death Sentence. Even if Q hits, don't recast it to go in if your allies can't follow up from that position.
Senna.laning: Get vision in the brush first, then look for an angle to hit Thresh Q Death Sentence where Senna steps forward to collect souls. If you can't control the brush, protect your carry's CS and collect souls with Thresh P Damnation. Don't risk picking up souls within Senna's range; retrieve them with Thresh W Dark Passage or give them up.
Senna.phase: Early on, pressure Senna while her health is low to deny Mist collection. Thresh should push her out of lane rather than overcommit to a kill. Soul collection remains important for both champions in mid game, so contest the spots where Senna collects souls while gathering them with Thresh P Damnation. In late game, Senna's attack damage and range increase as she collects souls, so don't approach carelessly in open areas.
Senna.teamfight: When you see Senna E Curse of the Black Mist, back off to a place with vision or cast an area-of-effect ability into its area to deny an engage angle. If your carry is threatened, peel with Thresh E Flay and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, look for an angle to catch Senna with Thresh Q Death Sentence and block her path with Thresh R The Box.
Senna.watch: Senna W Last Embrace takes time to root after it hits, so move away from your allies when you are marked. Stand behind minions to block W, and get out of the straight line where Senna Q Piercing Darkness can travel. If Senna hits you once, back off to avoid taking a second attack and deny her Mist collection.

Seraphine.build: Seraphine deals mostly magic damage, and Thresh has relatively low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. Buy Null-Magic Mantle early and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. If the enemy composition lets Seraphine lock down and pick off your carries, buy Mikael's Blessing; if healing from Seraphine W Surround Sound prolongs fights, consider Oblivion Orb.
Seraphine.combo: After Seraphine E Beat Drop is used, hit Thresh Q Death Sentence, land a basic attack, then pull her toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block her escape route. Recasting Thresh Q Death Sentence sends Thresh flying toward Seraphine, so only use it when your allies can follow up.
Seraphine.escape: Seraphine has no mobility, so the moment Seraphine E Beat Drop misses is an opportunity to engage. Close in with Thresh Q Death Sentence and hold Seraphine with Thresh E Flay. Throw Thresh W Dark Passage if your allies can follow you in.
Seraphine.fight: Trade right after Seraphine E Beat Drop misses, especially when Seraphine is alone and away from her allies. Look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from the brush or an angle without vision. If you are already close, disrupt her movement first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Q. Save your basic attacks until just before the trade, then land them one at a time.
Seraphine.laning: Get vision in the brush first to create an angle for Thresh Q Death Sentence. If Seraphine contests the brush, back off, protect your carry's CS, and collect souls. Retrieve souls that fall within Seraphine's range with Thresh W Dark Passage or give them up if it's dangerous.
Seraphine.phase: Early on, Thresh can start a fight with Thresh Q Death Sentence. The goal is to push the opponent out of lane and collect souls. The available information isn't enough to judge which champion has the advantage in mid or late game. Thresh continues collecting souls after laning to build armor for late game.
Seraphine.teamfight: If your allies are playing behind you, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, target Seraphine with Q, but make sure they can follow before going in. Spread out to the sides so Seraphine R Encore can't hit an ally and then reach those behind them.
Seraphine.watch: Seraphine E Beat Drop roots targets that are already slowed and stuns targets that are immobilized. If you are slowed, first move out of the straight line in front of Seraphine. Seraphine R Encore gains range each time it hits a champion, so don't stand in a line with your allies.

Sona.build: Early on, hold out with Null-Magic Mantle and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Sona deals mostly magic damage, and Thresh has low magic resistance, so build magic resistance first. If healing from Sona W Aria of Perseverance prolongs fights, get healing reduction with Oblivion Orb.
Sona.combo: When Sona is locked into casting an ability, hit Thresh Q Death Sentence and land a basic attack. As the stun is about to end, pull her toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block her escape route. If you're already close, pull her first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Sona.escape: After Sona R Crescendo is used, the risk of being stunned is lower, so look for an engage. If Sona has used E Song of Celerity, catch her with Thresh Q Death Sentence and follow with Thresh E Flay to limit her chance to escape.
Sona.fight: Engage when Sona steps forward to apply her aura or casts an ability. Catch her first with Thresh Q Death Sentence from the brush, then follow with Thresh E Flay so she can't escape with the movement speed from Sona E Song of Celerity. In trades, pair one saved empowered attack with Thresh E Flay.
Sona.laning: Get brush vision early and look for the moment Sona steps forward. Keep forcing trades to make her spend mana on healing, but if you can't control the brush, protect your carry's CS and collect souls. Retrieve souls within the enemy's range with Thresh W Dark Passage or give them up if the situation is unfavorable.
Sona.phase: Early on, pressure Sona before she has growth stacks, push her out of lane, and collect souls with Thresh P Damnation. In mid game, keep collecting souls around fight locations and jungle camps. In late game, Sona's scaling and sustained healing make the matchup less favorable over time, so don't let fights drag on.
Sona.teamfight: Disrupt Sona's position with Thresh E Flay so she can't apply her aura to your group. If your allies can engage, catch Sona with Thresh Q Death Sentence and block her path with Thresh R The Box. If you need to protect your allies, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel enemies off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage.
Sona.watch: Sona R Crescendo stuns enemies in a line, so don't stand in a line with your allies when Sona steps forward. If Sona suddenly enters basic attack range, watch out for the empowered attack from Sona P Power Chord and create distance.

Soraka.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Soraka deals magic damage, so build magic resistance. If healing prolongs fights, buy Oblivion Orb early to get healing reduction.
Soraka.combo: When Soraka E Equinox is used, fight in this order: hit Thresh Q Death Sentence, land a basic attack, then pull her toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Follow with Thresh R The Box if you need to block her escape direction. If you're already close, pull her first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Soraka.escape: The moment Soraka uses E Equinox to harass or clear the wave is an opportunity to engage. Soraka has no mobility, so close the gap with Thresh Q Death Sentence and hold her with Thresh E Flay. Only recast Thresh Q Death Sentence from a position where your allies can follow.
Soraka.fight: Engage as soon as Soraka E Equinox is used. Look for Thresh Q Death Sentence from the brush or an angle without vision. If you're already close, pull her first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Q. Only recast Q to go in when your allies can follow.
Soraka.laning: Pressure the enemy ranged carry alongside your ranged carry to make Soraka use W Astral Infusion. Soraka W Astral Infusion costs her own health, so keep up the pressure while dodging Soraka Q Starcall. Get brush vision to create an angle for Thresh Q Death Sentence. Retrieve souls in dangerous spots with Thresh W Dark Passage or give them up.
Soraka.phase: Early on, Thresh can start a fight with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but focus on pushing the opponent out of lane and collecting souls rather than just looking for kills. In late game, souls collected with Thresh P Damnation affect Thresh's durability. Since Soraka R Wish heals all allies, concentrate damage in a short window when you have a chance to secure a kill.
Soraka.teamfight: If you can engage, catch Soraka herself with Thresh Q Death Sentence instead of continuing to hit an enemy who is being healed. If your allies are fighting behind you, save Q, peel enemies off your carry with Thresh E Flay, and shield them with Thresh W Dark Passage. Use Thresh R The Box to place a wall along Soraka's escape direction or the route enemies will take to chase.
Soraka.watch: If Soraka Q Starcall hits you, Soraka heals and gains movement speed, so dodge it. Soraka E Equinox can silence and then root you, so use your engage ability before stepping into its area and don't stay inside it.

Taric.build: Early on, buy Null-Magic Mantle first and choose Mercury's Treads for boots. Taric deals mostly magic damage, so prioritize magic resistance. If healing from Taric Q Starlight's Touch prolongs fights, get healing reduction with Oblivion Orb.
Taric.combo: If Taric E Dazzle is used, hit Thresh Q Death Sentence, land one basic attack, then hold him toward your allies with Thresh E Flay. Follow with Thresh E Flay as the stun ends, and use Thresh R The Box to block his escape direction if needed. If you're already close, pull him first with Thresh E Flay, then cast Thresh Q Death Sentence.
Taric.escape: The moment Taric E Dazzle is used is an opportunity to engage. Taric has no ability to create distance on his own, so catch him with Thresh Q Death Sentence and prevent him from getting away with Thresh E Flay. Only recast Thresh Q Death Sentence when your allies can follow.
Taric.fight: Dodge Taric E Dazzle sideways and trade after it's used. Keep your distance so Taric can't keep hitting you with empowered attacks from Taric P Bravado. Save Thresh's basic attacks until just before the trade, then land them one at a time. Time your next damage for when Taric R Cosmic Radiance's immunity ends.
Taric.laning: Get brush vision and look for an angle to hit Thresh Q Death Sentence when Taric is occupied with a last hit or casting an ability. Keep collecting souls, but retrieve any that fall within Taric's range with Thresh W Dark Passage or give them up. Keep your distance so Taric can't easily get into basic attack range, and protect your carry's CS.
Taric.phase: Early on, Thresh can start a fight with Thresh Q Death Sentence, but keep your distance so you don't take Taric's strong melee basic attacks. Continue collecting souls with Thresh P Damnation through mid and late game to build armor and ability power. In late game fights, stop attacking during the damage immunity from Taric R Cosmic Radiance and wait it out with crowd control.
Taric.teamfight: If your allies are fighting from the back, save Thresh Q Death Sentence, peel away enemies who get close with Thresh E Flay, and protect them with Thresh W Dark Passage. If your allies engage first, catch one enemy in the backline with Thresh Q Death Sentence. During Taric R Cosmic Radiance's immunity, use Thresh Q Death Sentence and Thresh E Flay to control positioning, then resume attacking when it ends.
Taric.watch: When you see the tell for Taric E Dazzle, move sideways to dodge it. When Taric R Cosmic Radiance grants damage immunity, stop attacking and use Thresh Q Death Sentence or Thresh E Flay to apply crowd control and let the duration run out.
